title: Test static-prefix route constants by reloading mlflow.server.auth.routes and restoring it
answers: how to test routes under --static-prefix in auth tests
reload routes module with STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR set
test UI route keys built at import time with a prefix
body:
Route keys in mlflow/server/auth/routes.py are built at import time from STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR, so a test that needs a prefix must reload the module rather than reuse the module-level map.
Pattern in tests/server/auth/test_fail_closed_flag.py: monkeypatch.setenv(STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR, '/custom-prefix'), then importlib.reload(importlib.import_module('mlflow.server.auth.routes')).
Restore in a finally block: monkeypatch.delenv(...) followed by importlib.reload(routes), so later tests see the unprefixed constants.
HOME and SERVER_VERSION stay bare; only the ajax-derived UI_TELEMETRY carries the prefix.
applies: Auth tests that depend on static-prefix-dependent route constants.
says: Dashboard telemetry requests fail when the server runs under a custom URL prefix.
Allow the authenticated web interface to work properly behind a custom prefix.
Web console telemetry calls return not found errors behind a reverse proxy subpath.
search: Testing static-prefix route constants in auth tests requires reloading mlflow.server.auth.routes after setting STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR and restoring it in a finally block. Because route keys are built at import time from STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR, tests cannot reuse the module-level map. Only ajax-derived UI_TELEMETRY carries the prefix, while HOME and SERVER_VERSION stay bare.
